interpretation: The source action library produced zero successes on both selected levels. Both learned programs reduce to the same index-tie-broken sequence [0,1,2]. All four target arms fail 0/16; this is not an informative test of adaptive structure transfer, nor evidence that the intended general mechanism is false.
action_grammar_scope: Researcher-provided 32 Halton placements plus 16 object-relative drop expressions. The search can induce branch structure and thresholds but cannot invent new primitive action expressions or optimize their continuous arguments.
prior_art_boundary: Program synthesis, adaptive decision trees, executable skill libraries, and learned program transformations are existing ideas. This implementation does not establish a new learning operation or novelty 7–7.5.
baseline_scope: The kernel model and fixed source-coverage sequence are same-data numerical comparators, not a full reproduction of HExA, FlowEvo, or state-of-the-art physics solving.

native_controls.interpretation: Native known-solution replay passes 4/4. A single published HExA literal placement succeeds on 3/4 tested source seeds. These are post-screen controls and do not enter learning or establish HExA reproduction.

decision: Do not scale this finite action catalog or report it as a learned branching success. Retain the working native carrier and source traces. Continuous argument/program generation must solve source tasks before a meaningful structure-transfer comparison. Existing generic program-transformation ideas are not by themselves the novel contribution.
